Sub-totals measured per area: production code (dadaia_workspace minus public/) +2026/-1833 across 56 files; public assets +864/-709 across 28 files; tests +1341/-343 across 46 files; specs +547/-2008 across 31 files. 16 source files added, 6 deleted (process_ancestry protocol + adapter, 4 retired/merged public skills), 2 test files deleted. verdict_reason:
No blocking security or privacy finding stands against 7cff6284. None of the five mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES triggers fires, and each was tested rather than assumed.

SECRETS AND PRIVACY -- CLEAN. The operator-specified scan over every added line (`git diff 62b8dd68..7cff6284 | grep '^+' | grep -iE '/home/|password|token|api_key|secret|BEGIN.*KEY|192\.168|@gmail|@hotmail'`) returns 42 hits, and every one was chased to a verdict rather than counted. All 42 are word-matches in three false-positive classes: (a) 'token' as an LLM context-budget unit ('~4k-token budget', '~1.8k-token stamped digest', '~33.5k tokens') or as a session mode token ('the PERSISTED token', 'BOUND_READ token'); (b) 'secret' as the NAME of the scan engine being relocated ('the secret-scan engine', '_SECRET_SCAN_RULES', `test_secret_scan_engine_lives_in_the_privacy_module`); (c) the regex SOURCE of the detector itself (`("private-key-block", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"))`, the github/slack token patterns) -- a credential DETECTOR's pattern list, not credential material. Decisive negative controls: the high-risk subsets each return ZERO hits over added lines -- zero '/home/' operator-local paths, zero '192.168' or RFC1918 literals, zero '@gmail'/'@hotmail'/operator-name occurrences, zero actual PEM private-key blocks, and zero assignment-shaped credentials matching `(password|passwd|secret|token|api[_-]?key|private_key)\s*[:=]\s*["'][^"']{6,}`. The specs/ additions (which carry the archived audit and backlog histo records, the largest text block in the range) also return zero hits on the same high-risk pattern set. No value is echoed anywhere in this report; nothing required redaction because nothing matched.

DENYLIST / PUSH GATE, RUN ON THIS EXACT RANGE -- EXIT 0. `dadaia ci push-gate-check` was fed the real pre-push stdin shape ('refs/heads/feature/0.5.2 7cff6284... refs/heads/feature/0.5.2 62b8dd68...') via the absolute venv binary; it reports scan mode 'operator denylist + baseline' and exits 0. No new object in the range carries a denylisted term. This is the control that historically caught the two privacy recurrences, and it passes unmodified here.

PUBLIC-ASSET PRIVACY -- [ok]. `dadaia public doctor` exits 0 and reports '[ok] public-privacy', alongside '[ok] entities-derivation: 9 Personas <-> 9 core sub-agents' and '[ok] codex:rule-corpus-reachable'. I did not stop at the tool's own verdict: an independent grep of all 28 touched dadaia_workspace/public/** files for private markers (operator name, /home/ paths, RFC1918 and 192.168 literals, every sibling repo slug -- [redacted]-*, [redacted], james-bond, demolition, aero-fighter, space-war, speed-run, [redacted], [redacted], [redacted] -- plus databricks, infura, .amazonaws, hostnames and emails) returns exactly 2 hits, both provably false positives: the English noun in 'A demolition (deleting a subsystem -- this repo's dominant release shape) is authored expand-contract', which is doctrine prose and not the private repo 'demolition-ball'; and the template FILENAME 'dadaia_workspace/public/data/dadaia-AGENTS.md', which matches '[redacted]' only case-insensitively. Four new public skills ship in this range and none leaks a consumer-specific name, path or host.

DEPENDENCIES -- ZERO NEW CVE SURFACE. poetry.lock is untouched in the range. pyproject.toml's ONLY change in the entire range is the single line `version = "0.5.0"` -> `version = "0.5.3"`; no dependency block, no extra, no constraint is edited. setup.cfg's only change ADDS two modules (cli.commands.help, cli.commands.panel_composition) to the import-linter `source_modules` list, which EXTENDS the layered architecture contract to cover the new code rather than exempting it -- a software-integrity improvement, the opposite of the contract-deletion risk I flagged in the 0.5.2 review. Because no dependency moved, this diff introduces no CVE surface, and per the operator's instruction I ran no pip-audit escalation for the out-of-range tool venv; the pre-existing MEDIUM tool-venv CVE posture recorded in the 0.5.2 verdict is unchanged and remains record-only.

TEST INTEGRITY -- NOTHING WAS DISABLED TO GO GREEN. The operator's scan (`git diff 62b8dd68..7cff6284 -- tests | grep -iE '^\+.*(skip|xfail|quarantine)'`) returns exactly 4 hits and all 4 are prose, not markers: an assertion MESSAGE ('matching stamp must skip the rewrite'), a docstring naming a historical bug ('the segment-router-silent-skip bug had to be fixed twice'), a docstring describing string parsing ('re-parsing "[ok]   "/"[skip] " strings'), and -- notably -- a NEGATIVE assertion that the silent-skip parsing is gone (`assert 'startswith("[skip]' not in src`). Added skip/xfail/quarantine markers: 0. The two DELETED test files were each run down to their paired feature deletion rather than accepted on the commit message: tests/unit/infrastructure/test_process_ancestry_adapter.py died with dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/process_ancestry_adapter.py AND core/protocols/process_ancestry.py (the dead ancestry chain, -443 LOC), and tests/unit/features/panel/test_build_panel_views.py was retargeted onto the extracted cli/commands/panel_composition.py. Crucially, the deletions are not merely paired -- they are PINNED: tests/unit/cli/test_panel_composition_home.py::test_process_ancestry_chain_is_deleted now ASSERTS both files stay absent, so the removal cannot silently regress. Same posture for the retired doctor rules: tests/unit/features/specs/test_doctor.py asserts `"TREE-6" not in _codes(issues)` while proving the surviving single rule (SPEC-DOC-004) still fires as an explicit ERROR and never a silent early return, and the SPEC-DOC-016 retirement keeps SPEC-DOC-027 as the one naming rule. That is one-rule-one-implementation consolidation with coverage retained, not silencing. Net test change is +998 LOC (+1341/-343) -- substantially MORE coverage than before. I ran the security-relevant subset live: 264 tests matching secret|privacy|injection|verdict|push_gate|pre_commit|denylist|session_store|help_digest|scoped_law pass, with 0 skipped and 0 xfailed.

THE ITEM I TREATED AS THE REAL RISK -- MOVING A SECRET SCANNER -- AND IT IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS. Relocating a credential-detection engine between modules is exactly the change that silently drops a pattern, so I did not read the diff and conclude; I proved equivalence structurally. Parsing the pre-move `git show 62b8dd68:dadaia_workspace/features/spec_context/service.py` and the post-move dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/privacy_check.py into ASTs and comparing the unparsed values: _SECRET_SCAN_TEXT_SUFFIXES IDENTICAL, _SECRET_SCAN_KEY_SUFFIXES IDENTICAL, _SECRET_SCAN_RULES IDENTICAL -- 7 rules before and 7 after, same names in the same order (private-key-block, aws-access-key-id, github-token, slack-token, generic-secret-assignment, private-ipv4, internal-hostname). The scanner FUNCTION body is byte-identical too: name-normalized `ast.unparse` of the old `_scan_file_for_secrets` and the new `scan_file_for_secrets` compare equal, so both detection layers survive intact -- the cert/key-suffix presence layer that catches binary key material, and the content-rule layer over decodable text -- as does the redaction contract of returning rule NAMES and never the matched value. Consumer wiring is live, not merely declared: service.py:28-29 imports `scan_file_for_secrets as _scan_file_for_secrets` from infrastructure.privacy_check and both call sites (service.py:637 and :697, the dead()-commit review gate) are preserved; a live interpreter confirms `service._scan_file_for_secrets is privacy_check.scan_file_for_secrets` -> True with 7 rules loaded, and a committed test pins that identity. Zero patterns lost, zero call sites orphaned.

THE OTHER SECURITY-SENSITIVE MODULES ALL HOLD. (1) features/spec_context/injection_policy.py (new, 86 lines) is a PURE decision table: it takes plain values and returns an InjectionDecision naming an emission kind, a context slug and a stamp slug. It performs no I/O, reads no env, opens no file, and -- decisively for the untrusted-input question -- it never COMPOSES content; it only selects which workspace-local emission the transport should build. Extracting a 4-branch state machine out of a 469-line hook into a testable pure function reduces the injection surface. (2) hooks/ctx_inject.py's content sources are enumerated and all workspace-local: TECHSTACK.md, catalog.json, index.md, the sentinel, and the new .dadaia/agentic/help-digest.md. No network, no subprocess, no shell; stdin payload is used only to RESOLVE a context name via invocation.resolve, never injected as content. (3) cli/help_digest.py introspects only the live Click/Typer command tree -- command names and the first line of each `help` docstring, i.e. static source text -- and writes to a fixed workspace-local path. It touches no environment variable, no subprocess and no credential store; I scanned the generated artifact on disk and it returns 0 hits for password|token|secret|api_key|/home/|192.168|BEGIN KEY|@gmail. (4) core/session_store.py's `new_binding_record` is the one schema author and persists only session_id, context, mode, release, runtime, pid, bound_at, last_seen_at and ttl_seconds -- zero credential material -- and it REMOVES the dead `is_stale` field rather than adding one. (5) features/chokepoints/verdict.py, the module that decides whether a PR is authorized, is UNTOUCHED in this range (empty diff); the only chokepoint change is an additive, pure, WARN-only `bundled_ledger_advisory` that returns one advisory string and can never block, honoring NO-LOCKS. (6) The new SessionStart startup|resume matchers point at the SAME hook command via the same `_hook_cmd` builder -- no new executable, no new privilege, no new content source.

THE PURGE IS A SECURITY IMPROVEMENT AND CLOSES MY OWN PRIOR FINDING. Commit 7cff6284 deletes all six consumed verdict handoffs under specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/verdicts/ and _archive/0.5.1/verdicts/. A filesystem sweep confirms ZERO surviving verdict files anywhere under specs/. Because `features/chokepoints/verdict.py::discover_verdict_candidates` reads the archived root as an evidence root, each survivor was a non-expiring approval credential that would still authorize any PR whose head or first parent matched its sha. This range takes that standing-authorization surface from 6 to 0 and brings the code into agreement with DADAIA.md 4.2 ('a survivor is slop'). It is the direct remediation of the CWE-613 LOW I raised in the 0.5.2 verdict, which I therefore record as CLOSED.

GENERATED-FILE LEAKAGE -- NONE. The range commits nothing under .dadaia/, no .venv, no __pycache__, no .pyc, no .log, no coverage or test-results artifact. The help digest is written to the instance's .dadaia/agentic/ (outside the repo) and is correctly absent from the diff.

BUG-SURFACE DELTA (operator standing order) -- REDUCED, and this is the clearest case in the recent series. The headline +37 net LOC understates it because the range also lands a NEW capability (the CLI help digest, help_digest.py + commands/help.py, 136 lines total). Excluding that new feature, production code is +1890/-1833 = net +57 across 54 files WHILE ADDING 965 lines of newly extracted single-home modules (injection_policy, scoped_law, memory_canon, rules, specs_tree, entity_doctor, panel_composition) -- meaning roughly 908 lines were removed from the old sprawling homes those modules replaced. That is a net-flat redistribution that converts duplicated decision logic into named, individually testable owners, not growth. Hard counters, each measured: the container shrinks 607 -> 367 lines (-240, -40%); the dead process-ancestry protocol+adapter chain is deleted (-443) and pinned deleted by test; TREE-6 and SPEC-DOC-016 are retired so two rules that had two implementations become one rule with one implementation; the never-minted BOUND_READ mode token, the dead `is_stale` record field and `_compare_content` are removed; three hand-built gc_check copies collapse into one SessionBinding owner; ci.py's hand-rolled first-parent walk folds into the single seam. Branch count falls (a 4-branch hook state machine becomes one pure table), duplicate deciders fall, and specs shed 1461 net lines to archival. Tests grow +998 net, several of them explicitly asserting that the deleted things STAY deleted -- the anti-regression shape the standing order asks for. The open bug ledger stands at 0 open (`dadaia bugs status` -> '[ok] 0 open bug(s)'; 543 total, 522 resolved). Nothing in this range is a puxadinho: I found no added flag, no special case, no second code path and no cross-feature reach-in introduced to work around a symptom. The two INFO items below are observations about the widened injection WINDOW and an instance-local stale digest stamp; neither is a defect in the reviewed tree and neither blocks.

findings.message: Positive / closed: the six consumed verdict handoffs are purged, taking the standing-authorization surface from 6 to 0 and closing the CWE-613 LOW raised in the 0.5.2 verdict.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-613 (insufficient credential expiration) -- **remediated**, reported as a security improvement.

In the 0.5.2 review I recorded a LOW: `features/chokepoints/verdict.py::discover_verdict_candidates` globs `*.handoff.json` under **both** the live `specs/releases/<id>/verdicts/` root and the archived `specs/releases/_archive/<id>/verdicts/` root, and `covering_verdict` qualifies any candidate whose `agent == "security-reviewer"`, `verdict == "APPROVED"` and `metrics.commit_sha` matches the PR head sha **or its first parent**. Every retained archived verdict was therefore a non-expiring approval credential.

Commit `7cff6284` deletes all six survivors:

- `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/verdicts/b0fd592e28f0f92e82a38a156d380574dadf2204.handoff.json`
- `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.1/verdicts/b333fe2ed362689ce949220fd51ed6d9fd188acc.handoff.json`
- `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.1/verdicts/e18eafc5c51d1d4969cf379351a73d817b970827.handoff.json`
- `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.1/verdicts/e37c066a5fc2e64816e3880e2ab33988ab0ee8f6.handoff.json`
- `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.1/verdicts/e85eb40a638b212c23b3396e29a8a30cdb51ece8.handoff.json`
- `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.1/verdicts/f22fcab9b368b7a4334194b2bbda3c0ce85432fa.handoff.json`

Verified independently: `find specs -path '*verdicts*' -name '*.json'` returns **zero** files. The code and `DADAIA.md` 4.2 ('consumed once by the merge and deleted after -- a survivor is slop') now agree in practice. The prior LOW is recorded CLOSED.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action required for this PR. To make the property durable rather than manual, the operator may later choose to have `discover_verdict_candidates` stop reading the `_archive/` root altogether (or have `covering_verdict` skip `_archive/` candidates), so a future retained verdict cannot become a standing credential again. That is a governance choice, not a defect, and should not be bundled into this release.

findings.message: The context-injection WINDOW widens: new SessionStart startup|resume matchers make ctx_inject emit workspace-local file content at session start, before any prompt. The content SET is unchanged and the trust boundary is unchanged; recorded so the widening is a deliberate, documented decision.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-829 (inclusion of functionality from an untrusted control sphere) -- **not applicable today**, recorded as an observation about a widened window.

`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/runtime_config.py` adds two Claude Code `SessionStart` matchers, `startup` and `resume`, both pointing at the SAME hook command produced by the same `_hook_cmd(workspace_root, "dadaia_workspace.hooks.ctx_inject")` builder already used for `compact`/`clear`. No new executable, no new argument, no new privilege.

The effect is that a fresh session now receives the bootstrap at the event itself rather than at its first prompt (the stated goal: 'a NEW session received zero context until its first prompt').

**Content sources are enumerated and all workspace-local** (`hooks/ctx_inject.py`): `TECHSTACK.md` (bounded digest), `catalog.json` (lean tldr digest), `index.md`, the sentinel file, and the new `.dadaia/agentic/help-digest.md`. There is no network fetch, no subprocess and no shell. The hook stdin payload is consumed only by `invocation.resolve(...)` to determine a context NAME; it is never emitted as content.

**Why this is not a finding.** Any actor able to write `.dadaia/agentic/help-digest.md` already has local write access to the workspace and could equally edit `DADAIA.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `catalog.json` or `TECHSTACK.md` -- all of which were already injected before this range. The trust boundary is identical; only the timing moved earlier. The digest itself is generated from static Click docstrings (see the `cli/help_digest.py` note below) and the hook reads it fail-soft, returning `""` on any error.
findings.fix_recommendation: None required. If the operator ever wants defense in depth here, the natural control is the version stamp the digest already carries: have `ctx_inject` skip a digest whose stamp does not match the installed `distribution_version` instead of injecting it fail-soft, which would also make the staleness note below self-correcting. Do not change this in 0.5.3.

findings.message: Instance-local, outside the reviewed tree: the generated .dadaia/agentic/help-digest.md on this machine is stamped v0.5.0 while pyproject is now 0.5.3. Self-healing by design; no security consequence.
findings.detail_md:
Observation only -- this file is NOT part of the reviewed range (the range commits nothing under `.dadaia/`).

The artifact on disk begins `# dadaia CLI digest (v0.5.0 -- derived from the live command tree; authoritative help: \`dadaia <group> --help\`)` while `pyproject.toml` in this range moves to `0.5.3`.

`cli/help_digest.py::write_digest` guards with a stamp check -- it skips the rewrite only when the current stamp is already present in the first 200 characters, otherwise it regenerates -- so `install`/`reconcile`/`doctor` will refresh it. The content is derived exclusively from command names and docstring first lines; I scanned the on-disk artifact and it returns **0 hits** for `password|token|secret|api_key|/home/|192.168|BEGIN KEY|@gmail`. A stale digest can at worst under-describe the command surface to an agent; it carries no credential and grants no privilege.

Related instance-only residue, same class: one pre-existing session record under `.dadaia/sessions/` still carries the retired `is_stale` field, written before the `new_binding_record` fold. Records carry no credential material (`session_id, context, mode, release, runtime, pid, bound_at, last_seen_at, ttl_seconds`), so this is cosmetic drift that the TTL reaper clears.
findings.fix_recommendation: Run `dadaia public install` / `dadaia reconcile` on this instance after the merge so the digest is regenerated against 0.5.3. Nothing to change in the repository.
